Options: B) Two or more computers to share resources and data
D) Hardware components within one computer
Explanation: Network: two or more computers connected to share resources (files, printers, internet) and communicate. Types: LAN, WAN, MAN, PAN, Internet.
LAN (Local Area Network): network in a limited area (home, school, office building). High speed, privately owned. WAN (Wide Area Network): large geographic area (internet is largest WAN).
WAN: Wide Area Network. Spans large geographic areas (cities, countries). Connects multiple LANs. The Internet is the world's largest WAN. Typically slower than LAN, uses public/leased lines.

Options: B) A unique numerical address identifying a device on a network
Explanation: IP (Internet Protocol) address: unique numerical label assigned to each device on a network. IPv4: 32-bit (e.g., 192.168.1.1). IPv6: 128-bit. Used for routing data packets.

Options: B) Forwards data packets between networks
C) Connects peripherals to a computer
Explanation: Router: connects multiple networks, routes data packets based on IP address. Home router connects LAN to internet (WAN). Also assigns IP addresses via DHCP.

Options: B) Maximum data transfer rate of a network connection
Explanation: Bandwidth: maximum data that can be transmitted per unit time. Measured in Mbps (megabits per second) or Gbps. Higher bandwidth = faster data transfer.

QuestionText: Wi-Fi uses what technology for wireless communication?
Explanation: Wi-Fi: wireless networking using radio waves (IEEE 802.11 standards). Operates at 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz frequencies. Allows devices to connect to network without cables.

QuestionText: Email is sent using which protocol?
Explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol): sends email. POP3/IMAP: receive/retrieve email. HTTP: web browsing. FTP: file transfer.

Options: A) Analogue to digital signals and vice versa
D) IP addresses to domain names
Explanation: Modem (MOdulator-DEModulator): converts digital computer signals to analogue for telephone lines, and vice versa. DSL modem for broadband. Cable modem for cable internet.

QuestionText: The Internet is best described as:
Options: B) A global network of networks
Explanation: Internet: global system of interconnected networks using TCP/IP protocol. World Wide Web (WWW) is a service on the internet. Internet ≠ WWW (internet is infrastructure; WWW is a service).

Options: A) Routes data intelligently to destinations
B) Broadcasts data to all devices on the network
Explanation: Hub: basic device broadcasting data to all connected devices. Less efficient than switch. Switch: sends data only to specific destination device (MAC address). Hub is mostly obsolete now.

Options: B) Combination of text, audio, video, images, and animation
Explanation: Multimedia: integration of multiple content types. Text, audio, images, video, animation — delivered through computers or electronic devices. Used in education, entertainment, communication.

Options: B) Short-range wireless communication between devices
Explanation: Bluetooth: short-range wireless (typically 10m). Connects headphones, keyboards, mice, smartphones, printers. Uses 2.4 GHz radio. Lower power than Wi-Fi. PAN (Personal Area Network).

QuestionText: Encryption in networking is used to:
Options: B) Secure data by encoding it so only authorised parties can read it
Explanation: Encryption: converts data to unreadable format (ciphertext). Only those with key can decrypt. HTTPS uses SSL/TLS encryption. Protects sensitive data (passwords, banking) in transit.

QuestionText: A 'switch' in networking is better than a hub because it:
Options: B) Sends data only to the specific destination device (not all)
D) Connects to the internet directly
Explanation: Switch: uses MAC address tables to send data only to intended device. More efficient, secure, and faster than hub. Reduces network congestion. Foundation of modern LANs.

QuestionText: The TCP/IP protocol is used for:
Options: B) Communication rules governing internet data transmission
Explanation: TCP/IP: suite of communication protocols governing internet data transmission. TCP: ensures reliable, ordered delivery. IP: addressing and routing. The foundation of the internet.

Options: A) Physically protects servers from fire
B) Monitors and filters network traffic based on security rules
Explanation: Firewall: security system (hardware or software) monitoring and controlling incoming/outgoing network traffic based on security rules. Protects network from unauthorized access and attacks.
MAN: Metropolitan Area Network. Covers a city or large campus. Larger than LAN, smaller than WAN. Cable TV networks are examples. Connects multiple LANs in a metropolitan area.

Options: A) Computing using actual clouds for storage
B) Delivering computing services (storage, software, servers) over the internet
Explanation: Cloud computing: on-demand computing resources (storage, processing, software) over the internet. Pay-as-you-go. Examples: Google Drive, Dropbox, AWS, Azure, iCloud.

QuestionText: Social networking sites are used to:
Options: B) Connect people, share content, communicate online
Explanation: Social networking: platforms for people to connect, share content, communicate. Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, LinkedIn, YouTube, WhatsApp. Revolutionised communication and media.

Options: B) Test connectivity to another host/IP address
Explanation: Ping: tests connectivity. Sends ICMP echo requests; measures round-trip time in milliseconds. Ping google.com → shows if connected and how fast. Timeout → connection issue.

Options: B) Internet access and related services
Explanation: ISP: company providing internet access. E.g., BSNL, Airtel, Jio, ACT, Hathway. Services: broadband, fibre, mobile data, web hosting, email. You pay ISP for internet access.

Options: A) A box for shipping computers
B) A formatted unit of data transmitted over a network
C) A type of file compression
Explanation: Packet: small unit of data for transmission. Large data split into packets. Each packet has header (source, destination, sequence number) + payload (data). Reassembled at destination.

Options: B) A service on the internet: web pages linked by hyperlinks
Explanation: WWW: service running on the internet. Web pages (HTML) linked by hyperlinks. Invented by Tim Berners-Lee (1989). WWW ≠ Internet. Internet: infrastructure. WWW: a service on it.

Options: B) Digital systems, networks, and data from attacks, damage, and unauthorized access
Explanation: Cybersecurity: protecting computers, networks, programs, and data from attack, damage, unauthorized access. Includes firewalls, encryption, antivirus, 2FA, security policies.

Options: A) Hackers physically steal a computer
B) Attackers deceive users into revealing sensitive info via fake emails/sites
D) Data is encrypted for ransom
Explanation: Phishing: social engineering attack. Fake emails/websites mimic legitimate ones to steal passwords, credit card info. 'Click this link' → fake bank website. Spear phishing: targeted attack.

Options: A) Search files on your computer
B) Index and search web pages on the internet
Explanation: Search engine: web service that indexes web pages and allows searching. Examples: Google, Bing, Yahoo, DuckDuckGo. Uses crawlers to index web, algorithms to rank results.

Options: B) Continuous transmission allowing real-time playback without full download
Explanation: Streaming: play media as it downloads. No need to wait for full download. Netflix, YouTube, Spotify = streaming services. Requires stable internet. Buffer = brief pause when data temporarily unavailable.

QuestionText: 'HTTPS' is more secure than HTTP because:
Options: B) Data is encrypted using SSL/TLS
C) It uses a different port
Explanation: HTTPS = HTTP + SSL/TLS encryption. Data encrypted in transit — protects passwords, credit cards. Browser shows padlock icon. All legitimate banking/shopping sites use HTTPS.

Options: B) Any malicious software designed to harm computer systems
Explanation: Malware (malicious software): umbrella term for virus, worm, trojan, ransomware, spyware, adware. Designed to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to systems.

Options: B) Acts as intermediary between client and server (for security, caching, anonymity)
Explanation: Proxy server: intermediary. Client requests go through proxy → proxy forwards to server → returns response. Benefits: anonymity (hides client IP), content filtering, caching (speeds up repeated requests).

VPN (Virtual Private Network): encrypted tunnel over public internet. Provides privacy (hides IP), security (encrypts traffic), allows remote access to private networks. Used by businesses and privacy-conscious users.

Options: B) Digital audio content distributed via internet for download/streaming
Explanation: Podcast: episodic series of digital audio files (sometimes video). Available to subscribe and download/stream. Growing medium for education, news, entertainment.

QuestionText: The 'bandwidth' difference between 100 Mbps and 1 Gbps:
Explanation: 1 Gbps = 1000 Mbps = 10 × 100 Mbps. 1 Gbps is 10 times faster. Gbps (Gigabits per second), Mbps (Megabits per second). 1 Gbps = 1000 Mbps.

Options: B) High-speed internet connection always active
Explanation: Broadband: high-speed always-on internet (vs dial-up which was slow and temporary). Types: DSL (phone line), cable, fibre optic, satellite, mobile (4G/5G). Faster than 256 Kbps by definition.

Options: B) The physical or logical arrangement of nodes in a network
Explanation: Network topology: arrangement of nodes (computers, devices) and connections. Physical topology: actual physical layout. Types: Bus, Star, Ring, Mesh, Tree, Hybrid.

QuestionText: Star topology has all devices connected to:
Options: B) A central hub or switch
Explanation: Star topology: all devices connect to central hub/switch. Most common in modern LANs. Advantage: one cable fails → only that device affected. Disadvantage: hub/switch failure = entire network down.

Options: B) A small file stored by websites on your browser to remember information
Explanation: Cookie: small text file stored by website in browser. Remembers: login status, preferences, shopping cart items. Session cookie: deleted when browser closes. Persistent: stays longer. Privacy concern.

Options: B) 5G provides much faster speeds and lower latency than 4G
D) 4G is more widely available than 5G everywhere
Explanation: 5G: fifth generation mobile network. Much faster than 4G (up to 20 Gbps vs 100 Mbps). Ultra-low latency (<1ms vs 50ms). Enables IoT, smart cities, autonomous vehicles. Still being deployed globally.
IoT (Internet of Things): network of physical devices (smart TV, thermostat, refrigerator, wearables) connected to internet. Collect and share data. Smart homes, industry 4.0.

Options: B) ISPs must treat all internet traffic equally (no throttling or blocking)
D) All websites load at the same speed always
Explanation: Net neutrality: principle that ISPs must treat all internet data equally — can't block, throttle, or charge more for specific websites/services. Controversial policy debate globally.

Options: B) Unsolicited bulk email (often advertising or scams)
Explanation: Spam: unwanted, unsolicited bulk email. Often advertising, phishing, or scams. Spam filters in email clients/servers block most spam. Estimated 45% of all email traffic is spam.
Tim Berners-Lee: invented WWW in 1989 at CERN. First web server 1990. Father of World Wide Web. Vint Cerf: co-inventor of TCP/IP ('Father of the Internet'). Bill Gates: Microsoft.

Options: B) Download = data from server to device; Upload = data from device to server
C) Download = sending data; Upload = receiving
Explanation: Download: receive data (streaming video, getting files). Upload: send data (posting photos, sending email). Most home connections have faster download than upload speed (asymmetric).

Options: B) Malware that encrypts files and demands payment for decryption
Explanation: Ransomware: encrypts victim's files → demands cryptocurrency ransom for decryption key. Growing threat. Prevention: regular backups, updated software, antivirus, not clicking suspicious links.

Options: B) Very short-range wireless communication (a few centimetres)
Explanation: NFC: wireless communication within ~4 cm. Used for: contactless payments (Google Pay, Apple Pay, UPI tap), access cards, data sharing between phones. No pairing needed (unlike Bluetooth).

Options: B) ISP intentionally slowing down internet connection
D) Compressing data for faster transfer
Explanation: Throttling: ISP deliberately slows your internet speed (e.g., after reaching data limit, or for certain services). VPNs can sometimes bypass throttling. Related to net neutrality debate.

QuestionText: Which device assigns IP addresses to devices on a network automatically?
Options: B) DHCP server (often built into router)
Explanation: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) server automatically assigns IP addresses to devices joining the network. Home routers include a DHCP server. Prevents manual IP configuration.

QuestionText: The full form of Wi-Fi is:
Options: D) It has no full form — just a brand name
Explanation: Wi-Fi has no official full form — it was created as a brand name by the Wi-Fi Alliance. Often misattributed to "Wireless Fidelity" but that was a retronym. It is based on IEEE 802.11 standards.

Options: A) All devices connect to a central hub
B) Every device connects to every other device
D) One device connects to all others
Explanation: Mesh topology: every node connects to every other node. Most fault-tolerant and reliable. Multiple paths for data. Expensive and complex. Used in critical networks (military, backbone).
